extracted.intended_audience: writers, critics, editors, and students of literary parody and humorous writing
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing and evaluating literary parodies that mimic an original author's style while substituting surprising content; emphasizes intelligent amusement, faithful stylistic imitation, and an affectionate critical stance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intelligent Amusement
rubrics_metrics.description: The main intent of the vast majority of parodies is simply to amuse; but to amuse intelligently and cleverly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not mere mockery — clever recognition. The reader must know the original. Pleasure comes from spotting the substitution. Avoid crude ridicule; aim for wit that rewards literate recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style Matching (faithful form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful parody captures the original's syntactic/lexical patterns and replaces content while keeping structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parody should imitate the original's distinctive sentence rhythms, word choices, and structural habits so that the form remains recognizably the original even as the content is substituted. The form is paradoxically faithful: capture mannerisms and idioms to make the joke land.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affectionate vs. Hostile Tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Parody's tone ranges from good-natured affection to hostile contempt; most parodies are good-natured and show respect through imitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good parodies often demonstrate respect by the labor of imitation; decide whether your aim is affectionate critique or biting lampoon. Tone affects audience reception—affection tends to be rewarded, contempt can alienate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition (requires knowledge of the original)
rubrics_metrics.description: The parody rewards the reader who knows the original work; recognition pleasure is central to why parody works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parody succeeds when the audience recognizes the source and derives pleasure from identifying parallels and substitutions. Consider your intended audience's likely familiarity with the original when choosing targets and the degree of faithfulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitution Surprise
rubrics_metrics.description: The substitution of new content into the old form should be surprising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective comedic effect comes from unexpected content placed inside a familiar stylistic shell. The surprise should be coherent with the imitated style so that the incongruity generates humor rather than confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form–Content Tension (comic gap)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parody exploits the gap between form and content; the tension between the original's form and the new content is the source of comedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design substitutions that create a comic gap—the more a parody preserves the original form while inserting incongruous content, the stronger the comic effect. Balance fidelity to form with inventiveness of content to maximize comedic contrast.
